meta.column_notes: Raw Zeek tables use id_orig_h/id_resp_h/id_orig_p/id_resp_p. The alerts VIEW uses orig_h/resp_h/orig_p/resp_p. ts_datetime is string, ts is epoch double. All tables partitioned by dt (varchar YYYY-MM-DD).

facts.question_it_supports: Which source IPs generated the most connections today? / Who are the top talkers?
facts.proof_query: SELECT id_orig_h, count(*) c FROM conn WHERE dt='2026-07-25' GROUP BY id_orig_h ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 5
facts.notes: #1 talker is overwhelmingly DNS (see next fact). This is a stable, easily verified leaderboard.

facts.question_it_supports: Profile 172.16.16.16 — what is it doing? Is it a DNS resolver/forwarder?

answer.interpretation: This host is a DNS forwarder — ~99.9% of its traffic is UDP/53 to the two OpenDNS resolvers (208.67.220.220 and 208.67.222.222). Behaves like the NOC's recursive resolver.

facts.proof_query: SELECT id_resp_p, proto, count(*) c FROM conn WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_h='172.16.16.16' GROUP BY id_resp_p, proto ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 8; -- and: SELECT id_resp_h, count(*) c FROM conn WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_h='172.16.16.16' GROUP BY id_resp_h ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 8; -- and: SELECT service, count(*) c FROM conn WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_h='172.16.16.16' GROUP BY service ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 8
facts.notes: 208.67.220.220 / 208.67.222.222 are Cisco OpenDNS public resolvers — consistent with a DNS forwarder role.

facts.question_it_supports: I found my IP 192.168.131.7 in the data — what do you know about it? (by-IP profile, links to a critical alert)

alerts.name: ET INFO Android Device Connectivity Check
ET INFO Observed Cloudflare DNS over HTTPS Domain (cloudflare-dns.com in TLS SNI)

answer.critical_finding: This host (src=192.168.131.7) is the source of a CRITICAL notice: AWSServiceEnum::Possible_AWS_Service_Enumeration — 'Host appears to be enumerating AWS API service endpoints (5 services across 1 region within the last 1.0 min).' AWS SSL SNIs observed: dataplane.rum.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, vs.aws.amazon.com.

facts.proof_query: SELECT count(*) FROM conn WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_h='192.168.131.7'; -- MAC/host: SELECT mac, host_name, assigned_addr FROM dhcp WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND assigned_addr='192.168.131.7'; -- DNS: SELECT query, count(*) c FROM dns WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_h='192.168.131.7' GROUP BY query ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 8; -- SSL: SELECT server_name, count(*) c FROM ssl WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_h='192.168.131.7' AND server_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY server_name ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10; -- alerts: SELECT alert_name, count(*) c FROM alerts WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND (orig_h='192.168.131.7' OR resp_h='192.168.131.7') GROUP BY alert_name ORDER BY c DESC; -- critical link: SELECT src, note, msg FROM notice WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND note LIKE '%AWSServiceEnum%'
facts.notes: STRONGEST end-to-end scenario: IP -> DHCP hostname (Dikshya-stha) -> MAC -> DNS/SSL behavior -> a CRITICAL AWS-enumeration alert. Note: the alerts VIEW shows NULL orig_h for the AWS enum critical (it maps from notice.src which the view does not populate for this note type); to attribute the critical alert to the host you must query the notice table's src column, not the alerts view. Flag this to eval authors.

facts.question_it_supports: Are there suspicious/tunneling/exfil-shaped DNS domains? (threat hunt on DNS)

answer.cloudflare_tunnel: argotunnel.com — flagged 10070 times by 'ET INFO DNS Query to Cloudflare Tunneling Domain'
answer.notable: No obvious high-entropy DGA in the top set; long names present are legit (google clients6.google.com signaler shards, fbcdn netseer-ipaddr-assoc, office.com telemetry).

facts.proof_query: SELECT query, count(*) c FROM dns WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND rcode_name='NXDOMAIN' AND query IS NOT NULL GROUP BY query ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10; -- long names: SELECT DISTINCT query FROM dns WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND length(query) > 50 AND query NOT LIKE '%.local' AND query NOT LIKE '%.arpa' ORDER BY query LIMIT 12; -- tunnel alert: SELECT count(*) FROM alerts WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND alert_name LIKE '%argotunnel%'
facts.notes: The argotunnel.com (Cloudflare Tunnel) and namequery.com (RMM) domains are the best 'is this DNS suspicious' scenarios — verifiable against both dns and alerts tables. DGA-hunt scenarios are WEAK here (no strong DGA present).

facts.question_it_supports: What do we know about this MAC address? (by-MAC investigation use case)

sources.conn: id_orig_mac / id_orig_mac_vendor / id_resp_mac / id_resp_mac_vendor on every connection row — the richest MAC source (populated on ~all conn rows).
sources.dhcp: mac + host_name + assigned_addr + client_fqdn — maps MAC to hostname and leased IP (4937 rows).
sources.known_devices: mac + vendor_mac + host_ip + protocols + num_instances (2249 rows, 1008 distinct MACs). Corelight-derived device inventory.

example_mac_to_ip.note: same MAC also seen on its IPv6 fe80:: link-local

answer.caveat: Many MACs are randomized/locally-administered (vendor shows 'Randomized' or 'unknown - Locally Administered MAC'), typical of modern phones/laptops with MAC privacy. Vendor attribution only works for non-randomized MACs.

facts.proof_query: SELECT id_orig_h, id_orig_mac, id_orig_mac_vendor FROM conn WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_mac IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5; -- dhcp: SELECT mac, host_name, assigned_addr, client_fqdn FROM dhcp WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND mac IS NOT NULL LIMIT 8; -- known_devices: SELECT mac, host_ip, vendor_mac, protocols, num_instances FROM known_devices WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND mac IS NOT NULL ORDER BY num_instances DESC LIMIT 6; -- mac->ip: SELECT id_orig_h, count(*) c FROM conn WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND id_orig_mac='00:0c:29:3f:82:96' GROUP BY id_orig_h ORDER BY c DESC
facts.notes: MAC data DEFINITELY EXISTS and is queryable three ways. By-MAC scenarios are authorable: (1) MAC -> IP(s) via conn, (2) MAC -> hostname/FQDN/lease via dhcp, (3) MAC -> vendor/device-inventory via known_devices. Best golden-answer MAC: 00:0c:29:3f:82:96 -> 172.16.16.16 (VMware, DNS forwarder). Best hostname link: c8:6e:08:d6:0e:7a -> CSCO-W-PF5F1TWH.cisco.com. Caveat: heavy MAC randomization limits vendor-based scenarios.

facts.question_it_supports: Validate 'ET INFO Possible Kali Linux hostname in DHCP Request Packet' — are there real Kali hosts?
facts.proof_query: SELECT count(*) FROM alerts WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND alert_name LIKE '%Kali Linux hostname%'; -- corroborate in dhcp: SELECT mac, host_name, assigned_addr FROM dhcp WHERE dt='2026-07-25' AND lower(host_name) LIKE '%kali%' LIMIT 5
facts.notes: TRUE POSITIVE and cross-verifiable: the DHCP alert is corroborated by literal host_name='kali' rows in the dhcp table with real MACs and leased IPs. Excellent alert-validation + MAC + IP tri-linked scenario. (This is a NOC — Kali on the attendee network is expected/benign context, worth noting for the 'validate' answer.)

scenario_authorability_summary.by_ip_profile: STRONG — top talkers leaderboard is stable; 192.168.131.7 (Dikshya-stha) gives a full IP->host->behavior->critical-alert chain; 172.16.16.16 is a clean DNS-forwarder profile; 172.16.7.12 a bandwidth-hog profile. ~4-5 solid scenarios.
scenario_authorability_summary.by_mac: MODERATE-STRONG — MAC data exists in conn/dhcp/known_devices. 3-4 scenarios: MAC->IP (00:0c:29:3f:82:96), MAC->hostname/FQDN (c8:6e:08:d6:0e:7a), MAC->vendor inventory. Caveat: heavy MAC randomization narrows vendor-attribution scenarios.
scenario_authorability_summary.threat_hunt: STRONG — SSH activity, scan fan-out (10.220.250.29 by-port vs 10.220.250.18 by-dest), top-bytes talkers, DNS tunneling/RMM domains. ~4-5 scenarios.
scenario_authorability_summary.alert_validation: STRONG — MySQL scan (10.220.153.11->10.220.152.12) TRUE POSITIVE, Kali-DHCP cross-verifiable, AWS-enum critical (with the notice-table attribution caveat). ~3-4 scenarios.
scenario_authorability_summary.total_estimate: ~15 solid verifiable scenarios across the four use cases.
flags: The alerts VIEW returns NULL orig_h/resp_h for the AWSServiceEnum critical notice — attribution needs the notice.src column. Author accordingly.
alert_name strings contain spaced domains ('argotunnel .com', 'namequery .com') — use LIKE '%argotunnel%' not exact match.
severity is inconsistent free-text ('informational (default)') — exact-string match required.
DGA/high-entropy DNS hunting is WEAK — no strong DGA present; lean on argotunnel/namequery/wpad instead.
MAC randomization is widespread; vendor-based MAC attribution only reliable for OUI-assigned MACs (VMware, Cisco, Intel, PCS, AzureWave seen).
